Check detections, deployments and animals for data-entry errors

Source: R/check_detset.R
check_detset.Rd

Runs the data-entry and deployment checks and reports what each found. A check never changes the data: it returns the offending rows with counts and denominators, and the user decides what to fix. all_checks() lists the checks with their groups.

Usage

check_detset(
  x,
  checks = all_checks(),
  settings = check_settings(),
  water = NULL,
  field = NULL,
  reference_tags = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A detset(), or a list of plain tables detections, deployments and, optionally, animals, with the contract columns. Plain tables let the checks see errors that detset() refuses, such as a recovery before its deployment.

checks

Names of the checks to run; see all_checks().

settings

Thresholds from check_settings().

water

Optional water body: an sf polygon (water inside), or a terra raster of water depth in metres, positive down, with NA on land. A raster also serves the depth check. The two forms count differently: a raster tests only the positions inside its extent, and its note counts the rest as off the layer; a polygon tests every position, and every position outside it is on land. So a polygon must cover every deployment of the detset, or the deployments outside it count as on land.

field

Optional detection field for the two field checks: one number, the detection range in metres along a straight line; a de_field from the detfield package; or list(distances = , range_m = ), with a water_distances table from detfield and a range in metres. A field over some of the stations judges only them: detections at a receiver it does not hold are not tested, and the check's note counts them.

reference_tags

Optional data frame of reference tags: transmitter and their stated position, deploy_lat and deploy_lon. Their detections are not counted as unknown transmitters. When it is NULL and the deployments carry receiver_transmitter (see read_deployments()), those ids are the reference tags, each at the position of its latest deployment, with a message; an id the animals table also lists is left out with a warning. Give reference_tags to use your own instead.

Value

For a detset, the detset with the results in checks and one log record. For plain tables, the results alone. The results are a list of class detset_checks: summary, a data frame with one row per check (check, group, status of "pass", "flag" or "not run", flagged, of, unit and note), and rows, the offending rows of each check that flagged, named by check.

Details

Some errors explain others. A deployment whose latitude and longitude are swapped also lies outside the study extent and gives its station a second coordinate set; detections orphaned by a deployment date a year off also fall outside every deployment. Each such row is reported once, by the most specific check: swapped coordinates, then a wrong sign, then wrong units, then outside the extent; a year off or a time-zone offset before detections outside the deployment period. The checks that defer say so in their note.

Checks that need data not supplied report "not run" with the reason: the land check needs water, the depth check a raster in water and a deploy_z column, the two download checks a download_datetime column, the animal checks an animals table, long_after_release the setting max_liberty_years, and the two checks against the detection field need field. A check with nothing to test, a denominator of 0, also reports "not run".

Two checks catch a tag code entered wrong in the tagging records. transmitter_no_animal lists the transmitters heard that no animal carries, most heard first, so a code heard thousands of times stands above the stray codes of other projects; animal_never_heard lists the animals whose transmitters were never heard.

detections_after_download counts, per deployment, the detections after its recorded download (download_datetime) and before it ends. The deployment's data end at that download, so audit_listening() keeps those days "not_downloaded", and detset() marks the detections in the column after_download. They can mean a download time recorded too early, a later download missing from the sheet, a receiver that kept logging after the download, or a clock problem. Its rows give, per deployment, the download, the count, the first and last such detection and the UTC days they fall on. The check counts deployments whose download comes before their end; the note counts the detections.

Three checks read every transmitter: receiver_silent, moved_mooring and the co-detection checks. Cut to one species, the detections make a receiver that heard only other species look silent and change its co-detection partners; run the checks on every transmitter the receivers logged, reference tags included.

Limits of three checks, each measured on test arrays:

  • moved_mooring compares the stations that co-detect with a deployment before and after each date. With reference_tags, a deployment with enough co-detections of reference tags is tested on those alone; the others are tested on animal co-detections, which also change when the animals shift their range, so their flags are candidates to confirm against field logs. Moves shorter than about two receiver spacings score below the default threshold: on the 600 m test grid, moves of 600 and 849 m scored 0.40 to 0.69 and were missed, and 1,200 m scored 0.87.

  • dst_jump sees only a step back in the order the receiver logged its rows. A jump forward is never visible, nor a jump on a receiver that logged nothing in the dst_min minutes before it, and a table sorted by time hides every jump. It flags or reports "not run"; it never passes.

  • on_land takes a position exactly on the edge of a raster cell as terra assigns it, which can be the dry neighbour, and a position on a polygon boundary as sf assigns it. The two forms of one water body can disagree at such points.

See also

all_checks(), check_settings()

Examples

study <- detqc_example
dets <- detset(study$detections, study$deployments, study$animals)
dets <- check_detset(dets, checks = c("duplicate_rows", "receiver_silent"))
dets$checks
#> <detset_checks> 2 checks: 1 flagged, 1 passed, 0 not run
#>            check status flagged   of        unit
#>  receiver_silent   flag       6   20 deployments
#>   duplicate_rows   pass       0 3297  detections
#>   receiver_silent: deployments that hold no detection of any transmitter,
#>     of those that overlap the detections' time span by a day or more
